page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2ms_v2 is a specialized instance configuration that pairs high clock speeds with an exceptionally large memory pool. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8573C core with 2 threads per core. The x86_64 CPU operates at a clock frequency of 4.2 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and support for hardware instructions including AVX-512 and AMX matrix operations. The machine is allocated 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding an unusually dense 84.0 GB per vCPU. It includes no bundled local storage and lacks discrete GPU acceleration, directing storage requirements toward network volumes.

Benchmark data reflects the instance's unique balance of high processor frequency against minimal core count. Single-core performance is strong, registering top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing and robust throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, parallel throughput is inherently constrained by the single-core hardware ceiling, resulting in low multi-core scores across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng tests. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks also show lower throughput relative to multi-socket systems, recording 21.36 GB/sec for uncached reads and 14.38 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, this core-constrained configuration allows organizations to dramatically reduce software licensing expenditures tied directly to core counts while preserving a large memory footprint. The primary architectural tradeoff is limited parallel compute concurrency in exchange for maximum memory density per core and strong single-thread execution. This profile makes the instance well suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching engines, ETL data pipelines requiring significant operational RAM, and enterprise applications constrained by per-vCPU license models.
description: Microsoft Azure FX8-2ms_v2 is a memory-dense, compute-frequency virtual machine powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Configured with 2 vCPUs across a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled, it delivers an extreme memory-to-core ratio of 168.0 GB RAM, or 84.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache along with advanced execution vector extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX for specialized matrix operations. There is no bundled local storage and no integrated GPU accelerator, requiring reliance on attached network storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core compute performance, as seen in Geekbench and single-threaded compression tests, contrasting with weak multi-core throughput due to the constrained two-thread limit. Memory bandwidth on large uncached transfers measures modest. The server offers strong cost efficiency for environments constrained by per-core software licensing fees, making it an effective choice for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and single-threaded batch processing.
